extracted.intended_audience: experienced long-form improvisers (Level 4 or equivalent) looking to learn/perform The Harold, in London
extracted.subtask_description: An advanced eight-week in-person course teaching how to perform The Harold long-form improv format, aimed at performers with previous long-form experience who want to form a performing team and potentially do a final show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite: previous long-form improv experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Only suitable for people with previous long-form improv experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven’t got previous long-form experience it’s best to do our level 3 and level 4 improv course first. You should have done our Level 4 Improv Course or a similar amount somewhere else. This course is not suitable for people new to improv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course aim: learn to perform The Harold format
rubrics_metrics.description: An advanced course to learn how to perform The Harold format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Harold involves exploring three different worlds from a fun opening and revisiting those scenes and characters to explore connections, patterns and themes that emerge like magic for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcomes: make the Harold fun, funny and thematically rich
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to help you perform a Harold that is fun and funny while exploring themes, emotions, relationships and deeper theatrical ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will teach a variety of styles and techniques for performing The Harold, giving you the freedom to choose what works for you and what you enjoy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching approach: variety of styles and performer choice
rubrics_metrics.description: We will teach a variety of styles and techniques for performing The Harold, giving you the freedom to choose what works for you and what you enjoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course offers different styles/techniques so performers can select approaches that suit their comedic voice; Hoopla's version will include unique material even for those who've done Harolds before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance / team-formation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: As we’re forming a team over the course to do performances at the end it’s best not to miss more than one session over the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you think you’ll miss more than one session over the course please wait until another time to do the course. You won’t be able to do the show if you miss more than two sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ll be starting each session at 7pm, and you may not be able to take part in the workshop if you arrive after 7:15pm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an advanced course and we’re trying to form a team, so please don’t book this course if you are likely to be late on a regular basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show participation: optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Do I have to perform in the show at the end? No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show is optional, and you’ll still get loads out of the course without doing the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class size
rubrics_metrics.description: What’s the class size? Average of 14 people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small cohort size implies opportunity for individual attention and tighter team formation for the end performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course logistics: dates, times, venue and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates: Every Tuesday for 8 weeks from Tuesday 15th September 2026, plus show on Monday 9th November 2026. Time: 7pm – 9pm. Venue: Charles Dickens School, Toulmin Street, London, SE1 1AF. Tubes: London Bridge or Borough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eight weekly 2-hour sessions culminating in a show; location and transport links provided to inform booking decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price and payment options
rubrics_metrics.description: Price: £255. Either payable all at once or £120 at time of booking and £135 when the course starts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can book and pay in two instalments; details on booking link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher qualifications and teaching style
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher: Liam Brennan. Liam trained at UCB and iO. He performs in The Two Horsemen, Velour and previously in Hoopla house teams ... Liam is one of our most popular directors for Hoopla’s new shows and facilitates Hoopla’s corporate training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liam’s teaching style is fun and encouraging, while also teaching you some awesome skills to make your improv great! His professional background and corporate clients (Google, Facebook, Accenture) are presented as indicators of credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for participants who have done Harolds
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I do it if I’ve already done some Harolds before? Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is going to be Hoopla's own unique version of it and there should be some new stuff for you.
